source_text.body:
Build software from a spec with Claude Code and review sub-agents
A commenter has Claude Code build from a detailed spec using code-review sub-agents, context management and automated tests while they supervise.
·
Apr 1, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
A commenter described using Claude Code in auto mode to build software from a detailed spec, with code-review subagents, context-management rules, and extensive automated tests running as it builds. The human role was supervisory: leave it to work, then come back the next morning, decide what to change or refactor, update the spec, and repeat.
How it went
They said this could be especially powerful for solo developers and could create strong productivity gains. But they gave no concrete project, metrics, or finished result, and noted it is only worth trying if you can afford the token usage.
Worth knowing
The main catch they mention is cost: token use may be high enough that affordability is part of whether this workflow is practical.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Build [what you want, e.g. a habit tracker web app] from the spec in [path to spec file]. Work in small steps, write automated tests as you go, and use code-review sub-agents to check each major piece before moving on. Keep your context tidy by summarizing progress in a notes file. Stop when all tests pass and give me a short list of decisions you want me to review. Ask before deleting files or installing anything unusual.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1s2ok85/claude_code_now_has_auto_mode
